Docket 1.3.121

**Docket is free to try: run a full audit of any site without a key and see your score, how many problems each area has, and the most important problem in full with its fix. [Buy it once](https://kerr-affiliate-hub.kerrco.workers.dev/buy/docket?src=release-notes), $349, or 4 payments of $87.25, to see all the others, the ranked fix plan and the markup to paste. 30-day refund, no conditions.**

- *The engine's log says where an audit's time went.* Each finished audit now records how long each stage took,
  and how long each outside data source took, in the log Docket keeps on your Mac. If an audit is ever slow, that
  line says which part, and you can send it to support.
- *A link a browser upgrades to https is no longer called broken.* A link written as http:// to a site that only
  answers properly over https, such as an old Twitter link, failed Docket's check and was reported as a broken
  outbound link. Current browsers try https first, so a visitor clicking it reaches the page. A failing http:// link
  is now tried once over https before it is reported. A link that fails both ways is still reported.
- *Twitter/X tags without a card type are no longer called "no card markup".* A store whose pages carry
  twitter:title and twitter:description, but not twitter:card, was told it had no Twitter/X card markup at all.
  The finding now says only the card type is missing, which is also what its fix asks you to add.
- *A mailing address no longer makes an online business a local one.* A job board whose contact page gives a
  mailing address, and nothing else local, was treated as a local business and told it had no local business
  markup and no phone number, with three more local findings. An address labelled as being for post (mailing,
  postal, registered, billing) no longer switches the local checks on by itself. A street address you invite
  people to visit still does.

99 checks across 13 areas.
